prompt: A fixed odd composite is tested by 40 independent Miller–Rabin rounds, each using an independently and uniformly chosen base. What does the usual false-pass bound describe?

options.text: The chance this composite passes every round
options.explanation: For this fixed composite, at most one quarter of bases are strong liars, and independent rounds multiply that bound.

options.text: The chance every number that passes is composite
options.explanation: A posterior probability also depends on how candidate numbers were selected.

options.text: A proof that a passing number is prime
options.explanation: The random-base test bounds error; it does not make every passing result a proof.

options.text: A promise that the first round rejects this composite
options.explanation: A composite can pass an individual round when its base is a strong liar.

workedExample: Hold the odd composite fixed. One random round has false-pass probability at most one quarter. Independence makes the chance of passing all forty rounds at most one quarter multiplied by itself forty times. This is a bound conditional on a composite input; it does not describe the probability that an arbitrary passing candidate is composite.
